questions.q: A 35-year-old farmer presents with a painless papule on the right hand that evolved into a 2 cm ulcer with a black eschar and marked surrounding oedema. Gram stain of the exudate shows large gram-positive bacilli in chains. Which virulence factor of the causative organism is primarily responsible for local tissue oedema?
questions.exp: Cutaneous anthrax is caused by Bacillus anthracis. Edema toxin = Protective Antigen (PA) + Edema Factor (EF). EF is a calmodulin-dependent adenylate cyclase that raises cAMP, causing massive oedema. Lethal toxin causes tissue necrosis.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman presents with a non-tender, indurated ulcer with a clean base on the right labia majora. Dark-field microscopy of serous exudate shows motile spirochaetes. She is pregnant at 10 weeks. Which is the drug of choice?
opts: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM single dose
questions.exp: Primary syphilis in pregnancy is treated with Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM single dose — identical to the non-pregnant regimen. Doxycycline is contraindicated in pregnancy. Azithromycin resistance is increasingly reported.

questions.q: A 45-year-old immunosuppressed patient develops chronic progressive verrucous plaques on the face and trunk over 3 years. Skin biopsy shows 'copper-penny' cells (Medlar bodies) within giant cells. Which fungus is the LEAST common causative agent of this condition?
questions.exp: Chromoblastomycosis is most commonly caused by Fonsecaea pedrosoi (most common worldwide), Cladophialophora carrionii, and Phialophora verrucosa. Rhinocladiella mackenziei (formerly Ramichloridium mackenziei) is actually a cause of cerebral phaeohyphomycosis — it is an extremely rare and almost universally fatal CNS infection, not classical chromoblastomycosis.

questions.q: A 55-year-old man with long-standing RA on methotrexate develops grouped vesicles on an erythematous base along the T5 dermatome. He is allergic to acyclovir. Which antiviral is most appropriate?
questions.exp: Herpes zoster management: acyclovir prodrugs (valacyclovir, famciclovir) are first line. Brivudine is a thymidine analogue with superior bioavailability and once-daily dosing, used in Europe as an alternative when acyclovir-class drugs are inappropriate. Foscarnet is for resistant disease.

questions.q: A 30-year-old male presents with multiple hypopigmented anaesthetic patches on the trunk and thickened greater auricular and ulnar nerves. Slit-skin smear shows a bacterial index (BI) of 3+. According to WHO classification, which regimen is appropriate?
opts: Dapsone 100 mg OD + Rifampicin 600 mg once monthly for 6 months
Dapsone 100 mg OD + Rifampicin 600 mg once monthly + Clofazimine 50 mg OD + 300 mg once monthly for 12 months
Rifampicin 600 mg once monthly alone for 6 months
Dapsone 100 mg OD monotherapy for 12 months
questions.exp: BI ≥2+ indicates multibacillary (MB) leprosy. WHO MDT for MB leprosy in adults: Rifampicin 600 mg monthly (supervised) + Dapsone 100 mg daily + Clofazimine 300 mg monthly (supervised) and 50 mg daily, for 12 months.

questions.q: A 22-year-old woman with lepromatous leprosy develops sudden high fever, erythematous tender nodules all over the body, iridocyclitis, and orchitis. The Mitsuda reaction was negative at diagnosis. Which complication is this, and what is the first-line treatment?
questions.exp: Erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL/Type 2) occurs in lepromatous and borderline lepromatous leprosy — characterised by immune-complex mediated inflammation, tender nodules, and systemic features. Thalidomide (anti-TNF) is the drug of choice for ENL in men and non-pregnant women. Prednisolone is also used but thalidomide is first-line for ENL specifically.

questions.q: A 38-year-old woman presents with a butterfly rash, oral ulcers, photosensitivity, and painful joints for 6 months. ANA titre is 1:640 (homogeneous pattern) and anti-dsDNA is positive. She has no renal involvement. Which antibody, if positive, would indicate the highest risk for neonatal lupus and congenital heart block in her future pregnancy?
questions.exp: Anti-Ro/SSA (and anti-La/SSB) antibodies cross the placenta and are strongly associated with neonatal lupus erythematosus and congenital complete heart block. Anti-Sm is highly specific for SLE but not linked to neonatal CHB. Anti-dsDNA correlates with nephritis activity.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with progressive thickening of facial skin, sclerodactyly, Raynaud's phenomenon, and telangiectasias. Pulmonary hypertension is detected on echo. Which antibody is most characteristically associated with this subset of systemic sclerosis and its pulmonary complication?
questions.exp: Limited cutaneous SSc (lcSSc / CREST syndrome) is strongly associated with anti-centromere antibody. While anti-Scl-70 is associated with diffuse SSc and pulmonary fibrosis, pulmonary arterial hypertension is the characteristic vascular complication of ACA-positive lcSSc.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman presents with tense bullae on normal-appearing and erythematous skin of the trunk and flexures. Nikolsky sign is negative. Direct immunofluorescence shows linear IgG and C3 deposition at the dermo-epidermal junction. Which antigen is the primary target?
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid is the diagnosis — tense bullae, negative Nikolsky, linear IgG/C3 at DEJ on DIF. The primary autoantigens are BP180 (BPAG2/collagen XVII) and BP230. Desmoglein 1 and 3 are targets in pemphigus. Type VII collagen is the target in EBA.

questions.q: A 40-year-old man presents with flaccid bullae, positive Nikolsky sign, and crusting around the nose and mouth. DIF shows intercellular IgG deposits in the epidermis ('fishnet' pattern). Serum antibodies against which antigen distinguish mucosal-dominant from skin-dominant disease in this condition?
questions.exp: Pemphigus vulgaris: Mucosal-dominant PV has anti-Dsg3 alone. Mucocutaneous PV has both anti-Dsg3 and anti-Dsg1. Pemphigus foliaceus has anti-Dsg1 only. Envoplakin is a target in paraneoplastic pemphigus.

questions.q: A 70-year-old man presents with a pearly, translucent papule with telangiectasias on the left alar base, gradually enlarging over 3 years. Biopsy shows basaloid cell nests with peripheral palisading and retraction artefact. Which histological subtype carries the highest risk of local recurrence after standard excision?
questions.exp: Morphoeic (sclerosing/infiltrative) BCC has ill-defined borders and perineural/perivascular invasion, making complete excision difficult. It has the highest recurrence rate after standard surgery. Mohs micrographic surgery is preferred for morphoeic BCC.

questions.q: A 32-year-old woman presents with multiple pruritic, skin-coloured papules in the axillae, groin, and around the eyes, histologically showing mature sebaceous glands connected to a hair follicle in the dermis. She is concerned about internal malignancy. Which internal tumour is classically associated with this condition?
questions.exp: Muir-Torre syndrome is an autosomal dominant condition (mismatch repair gene defect, often MSH2) characterised by sebaceous neoplasms (including sebaceous adenoma/carcinoma) and keratoacanthoma-like tumours with gastrointestinal malignancy, most commonly colorectal carcinoma.

questions.q: A 65-year-old man with a long history of chronic venous ulceration develops a rapidly enlarging, firm, haemorrhagic nodule within the scar. Biopsy shows atypical vascular channels lined by malignant endothelial cells. Which eponymous association best describes this scenario?
questions.exp: Marjolin's ulcer refers to malignant transformation (usually squamous cell carcinoma, but also angiosarcoma) arising in chronic ulcers, scars, or burn wounds. Stewart-Treves syndrome is angiosarcoma in chronic lymphoedema. The histology here suggests angiosarcoma in a chronic venous scar (Marjolin's variant).

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman with genital warts requests treatment. She is 20 weeks pregnant. Which topical treatment is contraindicated?
questions.exp: Imiquimod is classified FDA Category C and is contraindicated in pregnancy due to possible systemic absorption and teratogenicity. TCA, cryotherapy, and surgical excision are safe options in pregnancy. Podophyllin and podophyllotoxin are also contraindicated.

questions.q: A 30-year-old HIV-positive man (CD4 count 80 cells/µL) develops painful, rapidly progressing ulcers in the perianal region. PCR confirms herpes simplex virus type 2. Which resistance pattern is suspected if he fails standard acyclovir therapy?
questions.exp: Acyclovir resistance in HSV is most commonly due to mutations or deletions in the viral thymidine kinase (TK) gene, preventing phosphorylation of acyclovir to its active form. UL97 kinase mutation is the mechanism of ganciclovir resistance in CMV. Foscarnet (does not need TK) is used for TK-deficient HSV.

questions.q: A 12-year-old girl presents with a rapidly spreading erythematous rash with honey-coloured crusts on the face. Gram stain shows gram-positive cocci in clusters. Which toxin produced by the organism is responsible for causing bullous impetigo?
questions.exp: Bullous impetigo is caused by phage group II Staphylococcus aureus producing exfoliative toxins (ET-A and ET-B) — serine proteases that cleave desmoglein 1 in the granular layer of the epidermis, causing superficial blistering. TSST-1 causes toxic shock. PVL causes furunculosis and necrotising pneumonia.

questions.q: A 28-year-old male presents with a papule on the glans that healed spontaneously, followed 6 weeks later by a maculopapular rash including the palms and soles, generalised lymphadenopathy, and split papules at the angles of the mouth. VDRL titre is 1:64. After treatment with Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU, which VDRL titre change at 6 months indicates adequate treatment?
questions.exp: Adequate treatment of early syphilis is defined by a four-fold (two-dilution) decline in non-treponemal titres (VDRL/RPR) within 6–12 months. Complete seroreversion may not always occur ('serofast' state). A four-fold rise indicates treatment failure or reinfection.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman presents with pruritic urticarial plaques and tense vesicles on her abdomen and thighs during the third trimester. DIF of perilesional skin shows linear C3 at the DEJ. Serology reveals anti-BP180 NC16A antibodies. What is the primary concern for her fetus?
questions.exp: Pemphigoid gestationis (PG) is associated with anti-BP180 antibodies that can cross the placenta, causing transient mild neonatal blistering in ~10% of infants — which resolves as maternal antibodies wane. Fetal risks (prematurity, SGA) are also reported but the classic concern is transient neonatal pemphigoid.

questions.q: A 50-year-old diabetic man presents with rapidly spreading haemorrhagic bullae, cutaneous gangrene, and severe pain over the scrotum and perineum. Crepitus is felt on palpation. Which is the most critical immediate step in management?
opts: Urgent surgical debridement with broad-spectrum antibiotics
questions.exp: Fournier's gangrene is a type IV necrotising fasciitis of the perineum — a surgical emergency. The cornerstone of management is urgent and radical surgical debridement combined with broad-spectrum antibiotics covering gram-positives, gram-negatives, and anaerobes. Delay in surgery dramatically increases mortality.

questions.q: A 60-year-old man on long-term hydroxyurea for polycythaemia vera presents with painful leg ulcers, hyperpigmentation, and longitudinal melanonychia. Which mechanism best explains the mucocutaneous toxicity?
opts: Inhibition of ribonucleotide reductase leading to impaired DNA repair in keratinocytes
Induction of calcineurin in T cells
questions.exp: Hydroxyurea inhibits ribonucleotide reductase, blocking DNA synthesis. Chronic use leads to impaired keratinocyte DNA repair, causing skin ulcers (typically over bony prominences), xerosis, melanonychia, and squamoid atypia. Methotrexate inhibits DHFR; 5-FU inhibits thymidylate synthase.

questions.q: A dermatology resident is performing patch testing for a patient with suspected allergic contact dermatitis. Which reading schedule is recommended by the International Contact Dermatitis Research Group (ICDRG) for standard patch test interpretation?
opts: Apply at Day 0; read at Day 1 and Day 3
Apply at Day 0; read at Day 2 and Day 4
Apply at Day 0; read at Day 2 and Day 7
Apply at Day 0; read at Day 1 and Day 5
questions.exp: ICDRG recommends patch test application on Day 0, removal at Day 2 (48 hours), first reading at Day 2 (after a 30-minute wait), and final reading at Day 3 or Day 4 (72–96 hours). Some protocols add a Day 7 reading for late reactions (e.g., neomycin, gold). The standard schedule is D0 application, D2 and D4 readings.

questions.q: A patient undergoes photodynamic therapy (PDT) for multiple actinic keratoses on the scalp. The photosensitiser applied is 5-aminolaevulinic acid (5-ALA). Which molecule, preferentially accumulating in abnormal keratinocytes, is the actual photosensitiser activated by light?
questions.exp: 5-ALA is a pro-drug that enters the haem biosynthesis pathway. In rapidly proliferating tumour cells with relative ferrochelatase deficiency, the pathway stalls and Protoporphyrin IX (PpIX) accumulates. PpIX is the actual photosensitiser that, upon activation by red light (~630 nm), generates singlet oxygen leading to cell death.

questions.q: A 40-year-old HIV-positive patient on HAART (containing ritonavir) develops a widespread, itchy, hyperpigmented maculopapular rash 3 weeks after starting a new antiretroviral. Which antiretroviral is most notorious for causing morbilliform eruption with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS) in HIV patients?
questions.exp: Nevirapine (NNRTI) has the highest rates of cutaneous hypersensitivity reactions in HIV patients, including morbilliform rash, SJS/TEN, and DRESS — particularly in women with higher CD4 counts. The reaction typically occurs within 6 weeks of initiation. Abacavir is linked to HLA-B*57:01-associated hypersensitivity.

questions.q: A 55-year-old man presents with pruritic violaceous flat-topped polygonal papules on the flexor wrists and oral white lacy streaks. Biopsy shows band-like lymphocytic infiltrate at the DEJ with 'saw-tooth' rete ridges and civatte (colloid/cytoid) bodies. Which cytokine is primarily responsible for the keratinocyte apoptosis seen?
questions.exp: Lichen planus is a T-cell mediated disorder. CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes release IFN-gamma, which upregulates MHC-I on keratinocytes and activates Fas/FasL pathway and granzyme B-mediated apoptosis. Civatte bodies represent apoptotic keratinocytes. IL-17 is central to psoriasis pathogenesis.

questions.q: A 10-year-old child presents with grouped vesicles on an erythematous base along the dorsal aspect of the right hand, which recur monthly. He has had similar episodes since age 5. DIF is negative. Which condition is most likely?
questions.exp: Recurrent grouped vesicles on the same site (herpes labialis or herpetic whitlow / acral HSV) with a recurrent monthly pattern since childhood is characteristic of recurrent HSV-1 infection. Herpes zoster rarely recurs in immunocompetent children. DIF negativity rules out dermatitis herpetiformis.

questions.q: A 25-year-old male presents with painless, flesh-coloured, wart-like perianal growths that have been growing over 8 months. Biopsy reveals koilocytosis in the upper epidermis and a thickened granular layer. Which HPV types are responsible for this 'low-risk' clinical presentation?
questions.exp: Anogenital warts (condylomata acuminata) are predominantly caused by low-risk HPV types 6 (most common, ~90%) and 11. High-risk types 16 and 18 are associated with squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix and anogenital region. HPV 1 and 2 cause common/plantar warts.

questions.q: A 48-year-old woman presents with an intensely pruritic skin condition characterised by excoriated papules and vesicles on extensor surfaces, buttocks, and scalp. DIF of perilesional skin shows granular IgA deposits at the dermal papillae tips. Which HLA type is most strongly associated with this condition?
questions.exp: Dermatitis herpetiformis (DH) is strongly associated with HLA-DQ2 (>90% of patients) and HLA-DQ8 — the same haplotypes associated with coeliac disease. Epidermal transglutaminase (eTG/TG3) is the autoantigen. HLA-Cw6 is associated with psoriasis.

questions.q: A 22-year-old woman receives itraconazole 200 mg BD for a month to treat onychomycosis. She is simultaneously taking a calcium channel blocker for migraine prophylaxis. Which adverse interaction must be specifically monitored?
opts: Increased itraconazole levels causing QTc prolongation
Reduced felodipine metabolism causing increased risk of hypotension and ankle oedema
Decreased itraconazole efficacy due to CYP3A4 induction
questions.exp: Itraconazole is a potent CYP3A4 inhibitor. Felodipine and other dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers are CYP3A4 substrates; co-administration raises their plasma levels significantly, risking severe hypotension, ankle oedema, and reflex tachycardia. This is a well-documented and clinically significant interaction.

questions.q: A 30-year-old man with type 1 borderline leprosy (BL) who was recently started on MDT develops sudden red, hot, tender swelling of pre-existing skin patches along with severe neuritis. The existing lesions are upgrading. Which immunological mechanism underlies this reaction?
opts: Type IV delayed hypersensitivity with sudden upregulation of cell-mediated immunity
Molecular mimicry with peripheral nerve myelin
questions.exp: Type 1 (reversal) reaction in borderline leprosy is mediated by a sudden shift toward Th1 immunity — increased cell-mediated immunity with CD4+ T-cell infiltration and macrophage activation. This 'upgrading' reaction causes acute inflammation in existing lesions and nerves. ENL (Type 2) is immune complex (Type III) mediated.

questions.q: A 55-year-old man presents with a 2 cm pigmented lesion on the right sole. Dermoscopy shows a parallel ridge pattern. Excision biopsy reveals atypical melanocytes extending along the acral ridges corresponding to the eccrine ducts. What is the most common mutation found in this subtype of melanoma?
questions.exp: Acral lentiginous melanoma (ALM) has a distinct mutation profile compared to cutaneous melanoma. While BRAF V600E dominates in superficial spreading and nodular melanoma, ALM most commonly harbours KIT (c-KIT) mutations/amplifications (~15–20%), making imatinib a potential targeted therapy. GNAQ/GNA11 mutations are characteristic of uveal melanoma.
